name: Extracutaneous Mastocytoma

criteria.description: Histopathological identification of a solitary mast cell tumor outside the skin
Positive staining for mast cell markers such as tryptase and CD117 (c-KIT)
No evidence of systemic mastocytosis or bone marrow involvement
Presence of a solitary, well-circumscribed mass in extracutaneous tissue without skin lesions

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of extracutaneous mast cell tumor with positive immunohistochemistry and absence of systemic involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of systemic mastocytosis and other mast cell proliferative disorders.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Solitary extracutaneous mast cell tumor mass
searchTerms: single mast cell tumor outside skin
lump of mast cells under skin

pathognomonic.symptomName: Positive Darier's sign at tumor site
pathognomonic.notes: Localized urtication upon rubbing the lesion
searchTerms: swelling at tumor site on rubbing

common.notes: Itching localized to the tumor area
Transient skin redness due to mast cell mediator release

searchTerms: stomach upset from mast cell chemicals
digestive discomfort due to mast cells
GI symptoms from mast cell release

occasional.notes: Episodes of increased heart rate accompanying flushing
searchTerms: episodes of hot face and tachycardia

occasional.notes: Occasional loose stools related to mast cell mediator release
Non-specific headaches possibly related to mediator effects

rare.notes: Severe systemic hypersensitivity reactions triggered by mast cell degranulation

rare.symptomName: Bone pain due to local infiltration
rare.notes: Rare involvement of bone causing localized pain
Transient low blood pressure during mediator release

laboratory: Elevated serum tryptase levels may be normal or mildly elevated
Normal complete blood count and metabolic panel
Negative bone marrow biopsy for systemic mastocytosis
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing solitary well-defined soft tissue mass
No evidence of systemic organ infiltration
genetic: Possible presence of KIT gene mutations (exon 17 D816V mutation usually absent)
other: Positive immunohistochemical staining for mast cell markers (tryptase, CD117)

distinguishingFeatures: Positive Darier's sign on skin lesion
Highly aggressive tumor with destructive growth

redFlags: Signs of systemic mastocytosis (e.g., hepatosplenomegaly, lymphadenopathy)
Anaphylactic episodes or severe mediator-related symptoms
references: Valent P, Akin C, Metcalfe DD. Mastocytosis: 2016 updated WHO classification and novel emerging treatment concepts. Blood. 2017;129(11):1420-1427.
Horny HP, Sotlar K, Valent P. Mastocytosis. In: WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
